title: Surface suction gripper for gripping and holding flat workpieces, has exhaust opening in workpiece that is opened towards exhaust duct opened to spacer of discharged air

features.item: A housing with a grip portion designed as a hollow body for gripping
An electrically operated vacuum generating device in the housing
features.quote: The gripper (10) has a suction surface (30) that is connected to a source of a partial vacuum suction chamber (28).
features.note: The reference discloses a suction chamber connected to a vacuum source, but does not specify if it is electrically operated or located within a housing.

features.item: Exhaust air from the vacuum generating device guided through the hollow grip portion to an air outlet
A sound-damping device arranged in the grip portion
A suction plate with carrier plate and seal extending around the carrier plate
features.quote: The gripper (10) has a suction surface (30) that is connected to a source of a partial vacuum suction chamber (28).
features.note: The reference discloses a suction surface, which can be interpreted as a suction plate, but does not explicitly mention a carrier plate or a seal extending around it.

features.item: A grip unit with hollow grip portion, electrically operated vacuum generator, exhaust air routed through grip to outlet, and sound-damping in grip
Grip unit and suction plate combined in a vacuum handling apparatus
features.quote: The gripper (10) has a suction surface (30) that is connected to a source of a partial vacuum suction chamber (28).
features.note: The gripper (10) represents the vacuum handling apparatus, and it includes a suction surface (suction plate) and a suction chamber (grip unit).
features.refuted: The quote describes a gripper with a suction surface connected to a suction chamber, but does not teach that a grip unit and suction plate are combined in a vacuum handling apparatus.

features.item: Grip portion at least partially lined with sound-damping material
Vacuum generating device arranged completely in a first housing portion
Sound-reducing device in the first housing portion or first housing portion lined with sound-reducing material
Grip portion elongated between first and second housing portions with air outlet on second housing portion
Air collection screw upstream of grip portion in first housing portion for collecting exhaust air
Bent or curved air baffles downstream of grip portion directing exhaust air to air outlet
Battery coupling point on second housing portion with air baffles directing exhaust air away from battery coupling point
Grip unit and suction plate releasably connected via a coupling device
Grip unit with suction opening fluidically connected to suction chamber delimited by suction plate
features.quote: The gripper (10) has a suction surface (30) that is connected to a source of a partial vacuum suction chamber (28).
features.note: The suction surface (suction plate) delimits the suction chamber, and the gripper (grip unit) is connected to this chamber.
features.refuted: The quote mentions a suction surface connected to a suction chamber but does not teach a suction opening fluidically connected to a suction chamber delimited by a suction plate.

claims.quote: The gripper (10) has a suction surface (30) that is connected to a source of a partial vacuum suction chamber (28).
claims.note: The reference discloses a gripper with a suction surface and a vacuum source, which is a component of a vacuum hand-operated laying device, but does not explicitly mention the grip unit or the laying device itself.

claims.quote: The gripper (10) has a suction surface (30) that is connected to a source of a partial vacuum suction chamber (28).
claims.note: The reference discloses a gripper with a suction surface and a vacuum source, which implies a housing, but does not explicitly mention a grip portion or an electrically operated vacuum generating device.
The reference does not describe the grip portion as a hollow body.

claims.quote: The exhaust opening in the workpiece (48) is opened towards an exhaust duct (22) opened to spacer of discharged air.
claims.note: The reference mentions an exhaust duct for discharged air, but does not specify that this air is guided through a grip portion or that a sound-damping device is arranged within it.
The reference describes a suction gripper with an exhaust duct for discharged air but does not mention a sound-damping device in a grip portion.
The reference does not mention a grip portion being lined with a sound-damping material.
The reference describes a suction gripper and a vacuum generator but does not specify its arrangement within a housing portion or the concept of a 'first housing portion'.
The reference does not mention a sound-reducing device in a housing portion or a housing portion being lined with sound-reducing material.

This reference describes a surface suction gripper for workpieces, not a grip unit with an elongated grip portion between first and second housing portions, nor an air outlet arranged on a second housing portion.
This reference does not describe an air collection device in the form of an air collection screw arranged upstream of a grip portion in a first housing portion.
This reference does not describe a grip unit with bent or curved air baffles arranged downstream of a grip portion in a second housing portion for guiding exhaust air to an air outlet.
This reference does not describe a battery coupling point for an electrical energy storage device or rechargeable battery arranged on a housing or second housing portion.
This reference describes an exhaust air duct for directing ejected air, but it does not mention air baffles specifically for directing exhaust air away from a battery coupling point.
(non-English passage at claim 1) The reference discloses a surface suction gripper for gripping and holding flat workpieces, which is a type of vacuum handling apparatus.
The reference describes a suction surface but does not explicitly mention a carrier plate with a seal fastened to it and extending around it.

However, the full claim 1 of the subject invention is not provided, so a complete assessment of 'said grip unit according to claim 1' cannot be made.
The reference describes a surface suction gripper but does not mention a grip unit or a coupling device for releasably connecting a grip unit and a suction plate.

claims.quote: The gripper (10) has a suction surface (30) that is connected to a source of a partial vacuum suction chamber (28). The suction openings and air jetting-end exhaust opening are formed on the suction surface.
claims.note: The reference describes a gripper with a suction surface and suction openings connected to a suction chamber to generate a vacuum for gripping workpieces.
claims.refuted: The quote describes a suction surface connected to a suction chamber, but does not teach a 'grip unit' with a suction opening 'fluidically connected to a suction chamber delimited by the suction plate' as claimed.
